about.title: San Fernando Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: San Fernando's mix of small manufacturing shops, warehouses, retail spaces, and delivery routes along corridors like San Fernando Road and Glenoaks Boulevard means workplace injuries happen in a lot of different settings. Some are straightforward slips or equipment accidents; others involve a delivery driver, a subcontractor, or a piece of faulty machinery from a company that isn't your employer. California generally routes workplace injuries through workers' compensation, but that system doesn't always cover everything you've lost, and it isn't the only path available when someone outside your employer shares the blame. We handle workplace injury claims directly — our team can look at the full picture, including whether a third-party claim might apply alongside your workers' comp case. Getting a second set of eyes on your situation costs nothing and doesn't obligate you to anything.

whyChoose.title: Why San Fernando Workers Choose Us

items.title: We Help You See the Whole Picture
items.desc: Workers' comp is usually the exclusive remedy against your employer regardless of fault, but that doesn't rule out a separate claim against a negligent third party like a subcontractor, property owner, or equipment maker. Our team can help sort out which path — or both — may apply to your situation.

items.title: Timing Matters, and We Help You Move Quickly
items.desc: California generally requires reporting a workplace injury to your employer within 30 days, and any third-party claim carries its own two-year deadline. Contacting us early gives you more room to protect both types of claims before deadlines close in.

items.title: Retaliation Is Illegal, and You Don't Face It Alone
items.desc: It's against California law for an employer to punish you for reporting an injury or pursuing a claim. If you're worried about your job while dealing with an injury, we can advise you on your rights without any cost to start the conversation.

items.question: I was hurt on the job near Truman Street — do I file workers' comp or a lawsuit?
items.answer: In most cases, workers' comp is your primary route against your employer, regardless of who was at fault. But if a third party — like another driver, a subcontractor, or an equipment manufacturer — contributed to the accident, you may also have a separate injury claim. We can review the details of what happened on or near Truman Street and tell you which options apply.

items.question: How long do I have to report my injury to my employer?
items.answer: California generally requires you to report a workplace injury to your employer within 30 days. Missing that window can complicate your workers' comp claim, so it's best to report as soon as you're able and document what happened.

items.question: Can my employer fire me for reporting an injury?
items.answer: No — retaliation for reporting a workplace injury or filing a claim is illegal under California law. If you believe you've faced retaliation, we can advise you on next steps at no cost to you.

items.question: What services do you provide?
items.answer: We handle workplace injury claims directly. Our team can evaluate your situation and determine whether workers' comp, a third-party claim, or both may apply. There's no fee unless we recover money on your behalf.
